collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A newer fisher keeps urging a villager to leave their old rock for the far rocks: try the far rocks, or stay put.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has fished from the same rock every morning for twelve years. (friend), who is newer to fishing, has tried to persuade (subject.him/her) more than once that the far rocks are better. "More fish, bigger fish! You're missing out!" Today (friend) is at it again.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: To get some peace, (subject) tries the far rocks. (subject.He/she) does catch more fish. Bigger fish, too. (subject.He/she) goes back to (subject.his/her) old rock the next morning anyway. "Why?" asks (friend), baffled. "Because I like it," says (subject). "The fish there are mine. The view's mine. More isn't everything." (friend) doesn't understand. That's alright.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "No," says (subject). "This is my rock." (friend) throws up (friend.his/her) hands and goes to the far rocks alone. (friend.He/she) catches lots of fish. (subject) catches fewer and has a lovely morning. They meet on the beach after and compare baskets. (friend) has more fish. (subject) has more sunrise. Both of them think they won.
